comparison.objective: Both move a carton while preserving free contents. Candidate selectively removes initially open-top cartons from a running belt and leaves closed cartons untouched; PR-1803 moves one carton with untaped bottom flaps from a table to a shelf.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate requires timed belt tracking, sidewall/body acquisition around top-flap interference, and level transport; PR-1803 requires continuous support from below so load-bearing bottom flaps cannot open.
comparison.success_condition: Both permanently penalize content loss and require stable released placement. Candidate additionally requires reject-tray routing, 3 s dwell, and untouched downstream passage of closed cartons; PR-1803 requires shelf placement and awards lift progress, with no classification or moving-belt condition.
comparison.reason: This is the closest record, sharing spill-free loaded-carton transport. The decisive tested mechanics differ: PR-1803 is specifically bottom-flap support against structural opening, while the candidate tests top-flap obstacle avoidance plus state-dependent interception of a mixed moving stream. The candidate still lacks a numeric flap-contact/damage rubric, but that does not erase these differences.
